exercises.title: Construct the counterexample data
exercises.objective: Choose discrete and indiscrete topologies and the identity map.
success: the proposed map is the identity

exercises.title: Check continuity and bijectivity
exercises.objective: Verify the forward direction without assuming inverse continuity.
success: the target contains the universal set

exercises.title: Refute homeomorphism
exercises.objective: Use singleton true to refute inverse continuity.
success: the proposed map is the identity

checks.message: The proposed map must be bijective; the identity is the intended witness.

checks.lean: example : LeanCraftGame.Topology.MyContinuous T9.sourceTopology T9.targetTopology T9.bijection := by intro s hs; rcases hs with rfl | rfl <;> simp [T9.sourceTopology, T9.targetTopology, T9.bijection, LeanCraftGame.Topology.discrete]
checks.message: The forward map must be continuous: indiscrete codomain opens are only `∅` and `univ`.

checks.lean:
example : ¬ LeanCraftGame.Topology.MyContinuous T9.targetTopology T9.sourceTopology T9.bijection := by
  intro h
  have ho := h {true} (by trivial)
  have hn : ¬ (LeanCraftGame.Topology.indiscrete Bool).IsOpen {true} := by
    simp [LeanCraftGame.Topology.indiscrete, Set.ext_iff]
  exact hn (by simpa [T9.sourceTopology, T9.targetTopology, T9.bijection] using ho)
checks.message: The inverse identity is not continuous: apply it to `{true}`, open in discrete Bool but not in indiscrete Bool. The data therefore is not a homeomorphism.

hints.hint: Every set is open in `LeanCraftGame.Topology.discrete Bool`.
Use `LeanCraftGame.Topology.indiscrete Bool`; only `∅` and `univ` are open there.
Use `id`, not a constant map and not `not`.
